notes.title: Summer Sale Patch
notes.content:
[p]Hey guys urb here, I hope the summer is treating you alright.
Rapid firing this one right after the big patch of DDay. It’s a slice from a bigger update that’s still in the pipe, but with the summer sale being on, I wanted to get some key fixes and new toys into your hands ASAP. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/e52129fdc3a0ea639ae4d081fb303cde679fb571.png"][/img]
[/p][p]This patch tightens up AI behavior, cleans out some code, and introduces late-game tactical directives that let you push back harder when the front starts to buckle. Classic players especially, you’ve got some new teeth now past wave 50.[/p][p][b]Highlights:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Sarge Call Check[/b] – You’ll now get a proper shoutback if you try to call in Sarge when he’s already boots on the deck.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Fuel Hit Cleanup[/b] – Yanked the .50s and R35s from the fuel system. Not everything on wheels needs to be a bomb.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Intel Drop Fix[/b] – Actionable intel drops more reliably now, even when you’re looting other crap. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Staff Car Auto-Spot[/b] – Enemy staff cars now get pinged automatically near your line. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Bridge AI Smarts[/b] – Pathing got a bump. No more troops suiciding in a straight line across bridges.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Bridge Spawn Logic[/b] – Bridges won’t drop right at map start or end anymore. Gives you room to breathe.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/fe142cfb16c942b9513111e3bb79e3ded5138d9c.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Magnum Ammo Fix[/b] – Magnum rounds now show up properly on the paper doll. [/p][/*][*][p][b]MP41 Touch-Up[/b] – Slight visual scale-up. Looks more like the subgun you should respect.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hardcore D-Day[/b] – No longer the default. If you want that hurt locker, you’ve gotta pick it.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Directives (x7)[/b] – Hit wave 50 in Classic and unlock combat directives. Force multipliers when you’re knee-deep. [url="https://urb-games.fandom.com/wiki/Directives"]Hit the wiki[/url] to learn about these one time use power ups.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Slugger Icon Added[/b] – Slugger perk now shows when frags or smokes get tossed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Debug Text Stripped[/b] – Cleaned up leftover dev text. You don’t need to see the wires.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Officer XP Fix[/b] – Killing enemy officers in Campaign pays out XP properly now. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Hold Fast Visual[/b] – Icon now triggers when Hold Fast kicks in. [/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7d1791826a9b1b2b73928fffcb83ccba428caeba.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Group AI Tweaks[/b] – Axis unit behavior got touched up now fights more in line with their type. Less random, more deliberate.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Manor Radius Fix[/b] – Manor now clears a bigger space to stop terrain clipping. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Faust Crash Squashed[/b] – Fixed a crash when 1st Div let rip with the improved Faust. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Some quick drops from the copmmunity:

[url="https://youtu.be/_3VKAO3bGN0?si=b2hqVM9YSahrkf00"]Check out Linus playing Some campaign [/url]

[url="https://youtu.be/X5hWZ2bJT3s?si=Q7L1E-jsmKD2rDtm"]Check out Sugar Bush pulling a 129 waves PR on Hasty mode[/url]

[url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msJy0JaIdEo&ab_channel=Skalar"]Skalar sneaking thru the end line in Master Mode!![/url]

[url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ze3KBzv5gpw&ab_channel=LanceNinjaace"]Lance's first Trench mode game, gg man![/url]

This update was a blast to work on. It makes fights more layered, more brutal, and just a little more streamlined when it comes to enemy actions. Thanks to all of you for continuing to push the envelope with your feedback and congrats to all of you trying for masters currently, very rewarding to see this level of skill at that scale. Don't hesitate to let me know what you guys wanna see next in the comments or in our discord.



Respectfully,[/p][p]– [b]urb[/b][/p]

notes.title: Mud and Blood DDay patch
notes.content:
[p][b]Good day folks urb here, 
[/b][/p][p]I'm glad to release this patch just in time for the 81st anniversary of the D-Day landings. This update introduces new mechanics to both [b]Classic[/b] and [b]Campaign[/b] modes, giving players greater control over their builds and long-term strategies.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/d1a304bb25f36d900a5f96faf4fad46b7e79bcef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The highlight for [b]Classic[/b] is a new system of power-ups called [b]Directives[/b], a mechanic inspired by what we observed in [i]Trench Mode[/i], which now enjoys a solid, dedicated player base. At its core, this system rewards perseverance and survival with powerful, one-time-use abilities.[/p][p]After some back and forth with the community, we’ve implemented a reward structure that kicks in every 50 waves. Each directive is randomly rolled with a rarity tier and can be [b]stored[/b] for later use or triggered immediately. They’re stackable, so if you're going for the Guerrilla Warfare ribbon, you might find it pays to hold on to a few.[/p][p]Currently, there are two types: [b]TP Surge[/b] and [b]Mass Resolve[/b], each with [b]five tiers of power[/b]. They pack a punch. At wave 100, you’ll get to pick between two directives. At wave 150, that becomes three — and so on.[/p][p]The system is designed to be modular and expandable, and I plan to add more directive types in future updates. As always, your feedback and suggestions are welcome.

We also got new enemies in this patch: 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/16619fed31d0471ef179861a0c9a2e2129b58414.png"][/img]
The first new unit is the [b]Feldgendarmerie[/b], essentially a German military policeman. These soldiers come with a slight health boost and, if positioned near a road, can [b]redirect traffic[/b] along that route making them a tactical asset worth eliminating early. Often used by high-ranking officers as close protection, they’re frequently armed with [b]MP41s[/b].[/p][p]Visually, they’re easy to spot: bright [b]red armbands[/b], long [b]green raincoats[/b], and a tendency to loiter near roads. While they’re [b]not especially brave[/b], don’t underestimate them when cornered, they can hold their own in a fight.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/911d98a8923037e1997e7e1747f6e3bfd5b47ac6.png"][/img]

[b]Puma:[/b] The Sd.Kfz. 234/2 "Puma" was one of Germany’s most advanced armored cars of the war fast, well-armed, and designed for deep reconnaissance in hostile territory. Historically, it packed a 50mm KwK 39 cannon, giving it enough firepower to threaten light armor while staying mobile on rough terrain. Its eight-wheel drive and relatively low profile made it a favorite among seasoned recon crews.[/p][p]In [i]Mud and Blood[/i], the Puma fulfills a similar role: a nimble, armored threat that shows up to [b]support light infantry elements[/b] and press weak spots in your line. Uniquely, it carries a [b]squad of Jägers[/b] strapped to its hull, who dismount when the vehicle reaches contact meaning you’re not just dealing with the Puma’s gun, but also a flanking infantry team if you're not careful.[/p][p]Treat it like a wolfpack scout if you spot it, assume there’s more trouble behind it.

Speaking of the volksturm they got a new AI coded just for them so they can move more as a light infantry detachment, exploiting gaps and probing with fast retreat. Let me know what you think but I feel ultimately all archetypes of enemy should have their entire dedicated AI routines in future versions.

We have a new map asset The manor:

[b]Manor:[/b] Large country estates or [i]manoirs[/i]  were a common feature of the Norman countryside, and many were repurposed by the Wehrmacht and SS as local command posts, supply depots, or officer billets. In [i]Mud and Blood[/i], [b]manors act as enemy strongpoints[/b], often housing staff officers, Feldgendarmerie, and elite units. These positions are not lightly held and may be defended with machine guns, booby traps, or vehicle patrols.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/c9e70c160e2749c414b337db688dfa8c2bda560c.png"][/img]
[/p][p]However, once [b]cleared[/b], manors are a goldmine. [b]Crates of captured equipment, heavy weapons, and valuable lootables[/b] can be found inside  a rare windfall for outfits like the [b]29th Infantry Division[/b], who are often [b]undersupplied and overcommitted[/b]. If your squad is low on gear, sweeping and securing a manor might be your best shot at resupplying  just be ready to fight room by room. The manor spawns in campaing with the new BC vultures nest. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/8de760e07a1e5ee513f09a43a90868693a0f7cde.png"][/img]

We have also bridges now: 

[b]Bridges[/b] appear in [b]Classic[/b] and at times in [b]Campaign mode[/b] under the [i]A Bridge Too Far[/i] battle condition. They are [b]destructible[/b], [b]provide minimal cover[/b], and take up a fair bit of space making them both a tactical asset and a liability.
[/p][p]Historically, bridges were [b]critical choke points[/b] during the Allied advance across France, and the Wehrmacht knew it. Expect the enemy to do what they've done best so far: [b]dig in on the far side[/b], mine the approaches, and [b]set up interlocking fields of fire[/b] across the span. Bridging a gap under fire is a brutal affair, and you’d better believe they’ll be waiting.

[b]In the [i]A Bridge Too Far[/i] battle condition[/b], your objective is to [b]rush forward and relieve an isolated airborne element[/b] tasked with holding a critical bridge until your arrival. The mission will [b]fail if all airborne troops are killed or if the Germans manage to destroy the bridge[/b].[/p][p]This setup creates [b]tense, cinematic moments[/b] and some truly [b]memorable war stories[/b] — reminiscent of scenes from the film of the same name. I’m really proud of how this one turned out, and I can’t wait for you all to get your boots muddy and try it for yourselves.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/d6a6dc43e06ba140babc0bfabf114a852d56fbb3.png"][/img]
[b]Since we’re on the topic of Battle Conditions[/b], there’s one in the Campaign called [b]Killzones[/b]. The premise is rooted in historical reality: [b]German forces, often lacking real-time radio communication[/b], would [b]pre-zero artillery[/b] onto likely crossing points, road junctions, or chokeholds. These areas were marked subtly  a disturbed patch of ground, stacked stones, a splash of colored brick dust and monitored by [b]forward observers positioned well outside your immediate AO[/b].[/p][p]At first, you won’t know what to look for. But after a few near-death experiences, you’ll start to recognize the signs. And you’d better because [b]stepping into one of these killzones is almost guaranteed to trigger a lightning-fast artillery strike[/b]. Veterans of the front learned to spot and avoid these patterns like their lives depended on it. In this case, [b]so will you[/b].

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/72498b4602e1ad1f03c05bb4202253748e628211.png"][/img][/p][p]
[b]There’s a new weapon in the game: the MP41[/b] a fairly rare submachine gun most commonly carried by [b]Feldgendarmerie[/b] units. Mechanically, it shares many internal components with the MP40, but features a [b]wooden stock[/b] instead of the folding metal one. This makes it [b]slightly bulkier[/b], but also more stable for [b]deliberate, aimed fire[/b]  especially when firing from the shoulder.[/p][p]Historically, the MP41 was produced in limited numbers by [b]Haenel[/b], and was issued mainly to [b]rear-line or security forces[/b], not frontline infantry. Its hybrid design combining the [b]MP40’s proven internals with a more traditional stock[/b] was seen as a compromise between modernity and familiarity.[/p][p]In-game, it comes with a [b]distinctive sound profile[/b], and you'll usually find it in the hands of German military police or officers' bodyguards.

[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/c9206b0ce7edc47b0c84fad3bca6c705f23e96ac.png"][/img]

[b]We’ve also added a new grenade launcher: the Leuchtpistole.[/b] Though fairly rare on the battlefield, this single-shot flare gun turned grenade launcher serves a specialized role — especially useful when you need to [b]lob an explosive through a narrow window or tight doorway[/b].

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/907bd380dd766d0448d1bef4af59d3aba4511b01.png"][/img]
[/p][p]Originally designed to fire flares or signal rounds, German forces later adapted the [b]Leuchtpistole[/b] to launch explosive grenades such as the [b]Wurfkörper 361[/b], effectively turning it into a lightweight, direct-fire launcher for [b]urban or close-quarters use[/b]. While offering better [b]speed and range[/b] of delivery compared to a hand-thrown grenade, it’s also [b]more cumbersome to reload and handle[/b], especially under pressure.[/p][p]In-game, this translates into a [b]capable but situational weapon[/b], particularly effective in urban settings where [b]line-of-sight is limited[/b] and [b]window shots matter[/b]. When looted from a fallen German soldier, it typically comes with [b]three rounds[/b], making it a valuable — if temporary — asset in clearing out stubborn positions.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/ddfcd0cd4fbf38e7d4ba052e34a0303a86627c77.png"][/img]

[b]Finally, I’ve added 21 perks for soldiers in campaign mode.[/b] These are passive abilities that subtly but significantly influence a soldier’s performance in combat. We're talking about things like [b]throwing grenades further and faster[/b], [b]executing tactical reloads[/b], [b]moving more quietly[/b], or [b]being harder to suppress under fire[/b].[/p][p]Perks are designed to reflect small advantages gained from experience, temperament, or training the kind of edge that [b]doesn’t break immersion[/b] or turn your trooper into a superhero, but makes them feel like [b]seasoned, capable warfighters[/b] in the chaos of battle.[/p][p]They’re also a big part of [b]customizing your squad[/b], encouraging you to pay attention to [b]who survives[/b], and how you want to shape your team's capabilities over time. Some perks are rare. Some synergize beautifully. Others only shine in very specific situations just like real soldiers.


[b]Finally, here’s the full list of features in this patch.[/b] [/p][list][*][p]Trench mode has a new airborne drop card[/p][/*][*][p]Blood footprints now appear when walking in gibs[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy master snipers will hide between shots — notably painful during Campaign[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where dirt roads wouldn't spawn vehicles or count as roads in the logic[/p][/*][*][p]Added the alarm item — when used, the side that activates it gets reinforcements equal to all non-gibbed casualties within a 300px radius[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Pak 36 not showing up in the Rat Pack BC[/p][/*][*][p]Added bridges to map assets across all biomes[/p][/*][*][p]Added BC Killzone, where Germans have preset artillery zones[/p][/*][*][p]Added BC Bridge Too Far, where you must secure a bridge before all the airborne troops die[/p][/*][*][p]Added Flak 30 to classic spawn tables for emplacements[/p][/*][*][p]Kettenkrads are now less obsessed with doing donuts before leaving[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where advanced support was called too early in Campaign when hardcore D-Day was selected[/p][/*][*][p]Increased the range and likelihood for Germans to target tents and supply depots with support[/p][/*][*][p]New grenade: Contact Grenade — explodes instantly on impact. Not great indoors, perfect for hitting tight formations fast[/p][/*][*][p]New German vehicle: the Puma — can carry up to 4 Jägers and deploy them into combat[/p][/*][*][p]Panzerfaust 2: now has better range, travels faster, hits harder against armor, but has a smaller frag radius[/p][/*][*][p]Molotovs, Blendkörper, and other throwable breakables won’t break in water — they can be picked up and thrown again[/p][/*][*][p]Added descriptive text to Bangalores[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Bangalore model angle — no more sideways deployment[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the MG RoF on Sd.Kfz and Kübels, making them proper infantry support instead of gunboats[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Allied vehicle decrewing only spawning the commander[/p][/*][*][p]Ace Tiger crew now grants +15 XP[/p][/*][*][p]Added a Manor — a large building where enemy staff officers spawn. Rumored to contain juicy actionable intel[/p][/*][*][p]Added a rare item: Actionable Intel — use it to flip Osttruppen soldiers to your side[/p][/*][*][p]Destroyed trap doors now provide improvised cover — basically a hole in the ground[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced debris size for destroyed trap doors[/p][/*][*][p]Broom function now cleans more aggressively to improve performance on lower-end rigs[/p][/*][*][p]Added failsafe to prevent off-screen Emplacements in Ashen[/p][/*][*][p]Shrek crews will now hunt isolated vehicles in late-game Classic — be advised[/p][/*][*][p]Shotgun-wielding Commandos now automatically slam-fire[/p][/*][*][p]Wire and entanglements will unstealth any troops caught in them[/p][/*][*][p]Allied troops stuck in wire may draw German support and ordnance fire[/p][/*][*][p]German AI now reacts more situationally to disturbed vegetation[/p][/*][*][p]Troops stuck in entanglements raise German awareness and trigger tactical reactions[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced Land Mattress signature by 25% (less counter-battery risk); increased staying time by 2 mins per rarity in Campaign; increased AT radius by 25px for Nebel and Land Mattress[/p][/*][*][p]Added new German unit: the Feldgendarmerie (MP) — tough, and able to direct traffic if near a road[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked squad menu medal display, especially for soldiers with large stacks[/p][/*][*][p]Replaced skill icons with perk icons in squad panels[/p][/*][*][p]Campaign now features a perk system with 21 new perks[/p][/*][*][p]New weapon: MP41[/p][/*][*][p]New lootable: Leuchtpistole — a pistol-shaped grenade launcher, especially good at lobbing explosives into buildings[/p][/*][*][p]New lootable: Alarm Kits — can spawn reinforcements for either side[/p][/*][*][p]Fliegerfausts are now operational and lootable from Luftwaffe soldiers[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy commander AI in Trench Mode is now more reactive to player behavior[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy HQs now have cooldowns to reduce vehicle spam, especially on D-Day[/p][/*][*][p]Added Directives  a game-changing mechanic in Classic mode with strong modular potential[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/c0321f92af7f85947745575736a9da1d7589df4e.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This one was a blast to work on. It adds a bunch of new variables to the mix, making every fight more dynamic, more brutal, and more satisfying both to watch and to survive.[/p][p]After two years on the stove, [i]Mud and Blood[/i] has racked up 49 patches. We’re now sitting on 11 enemy types, over 50 weapons, 35 vehicles, 74 battle conditions, 80 ribbons, and more than a few hard-fought stories of close calls, bad beats, and righteous victories.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/0baaf909c596a604eb3d3473a85ad02d905f1af7.png"][/img]

[url="https://youtu.be/f_WfZEd-5_g?si=HIb5B1KgZzx-j3eG"]Keep an eye on this one[/url] — looks like we’ve got a second [b]Mud and Blood master[/b] in the making. Running a D-Day landing on [b]Master Mode[/b] (the highest difficulty), clearing out a [b]Manor[/b], and dropping a few senior officers along the way. Plenty of close calls. At this level, one bad move and the whole squad’s gone.If you're into Mud and Blood, this kind of run speaks for itself.

We have other folks fighting the good fight here as well

[url="https://youtu.be/AUr5Q1jmeY8?si=cHSVhtp0AGnIGP_t"]MJ doing pretty good in Brutal mode[/url] (the mode right before Masters) it's worth having a look to see how MNB can be played at that level how and when to move.

[url="https://youtu.be/aVfKBs-UrSQ?si=TkJZpvmD3fPrXh_B"]Here’s War Panda running training mode[/url] and putting in the work. Nothing wrong with learning the ropes before stepping into the meat grinder.

[url="https://youtu.be/0K8BkF0GdZc?si=3rkxv78OKX_G-WGa"]Here we got Tutle[/url], always a blast to watch him maneuver and trade blows — especially in a no-intel battle condition. Pure grit, free ballin' across St-Lo.

[url="https://youtu.be/-jl2CuidHZ4?si=sPCvoB_kPhCU9Bq5"]New campaign player hitting the beach[/url] for the first time always cool to watch someone catch the rhythm mid-chaos. Baptism by fire, the grunt way.

Last but not least, [url="https://youtu.be/-jl2CuidHZ4?si=sPCvoB_kPhCU9Bq5"]it’s old Lance, punching through Brest one bloodied tile at a time[/url]. Him and I ain't top-tier, but we’ve been in enough fights to know which way the rounds are flying. Let them young masters flex — we’ll be at the old man table, trading scars ;)


That said, let’s all keep in mind that D-Day was quite the shit show in real life, and we’re all very lucky to be safe and playing vids when you stop to think about it. Let’s count our blessings sure enough, one of mine is being able to make this game for you folks. Until next time.

Respectfully
[/p][p]p.s. are we ready for Recondo or what?

urb


[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The Mud and Blood Demo has been updated
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/4a7e04b3a5f9870f62671caedad3beb01c42eb25.png[/img]

It’s been a while since we updated the [b]Mud and Blood DEMO[/b], but I’m thrilled to share the fully upgraded 0.4.8a version. With new enemies like Volksgrenadiers, Luftwaffe Infantry, and Officers, revamped Trench Mode, and overhauled vehicle mechanics, the chaos has never felt so good. This update brings the improvements we’ve been enjoying on the main branch for some time and is a great chance to introduce your gun-shy friends to the joy of brutality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/6b139d311743bf3c56a21b680389fafd79de36ce.png[/img]

On the full game front of things the game I've took the holidays to fix few things:

- Fixed a fault where the creation of a brand new profile would crash the games if it generated tip of the Spear or Rear echelon Battle conditions.
- Brand new profile will have hard core DDay set to "on" by default
- Added a catch for an exception generated by the steam achievement function
- Disabling main cannon on a SDKFZ222 will disable the 20mm
- Fixed a fault that made pak38s having fuel tanks.
- Fixed scrounger command ability to last one mission per tier of rarity
- FJs in trench mode will drop on any trenches in end games (on a many wins streak)
- Fixed the Siegfried ribbon in campaign.
- Fixed some typos (thanks Skaen)

We got some solid gameplay during the holiday season from our pro players and from some very keen new members let's check this out:

Check out Cheeks [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pt72FPR_UUY&ab_channel=cheekibreeki]dropping on DDay in unfair mode[/url] (NG++) and finishing with all his troops but not without a tough fight. in 9 mins mind you.

For some learning on how to [url=https://youtu.be/KrdvtCHV2bY?si=hIcdKAL3Jvq_Ypfs]move properly with or without armor support[/url], my fav is Tutle with this Hedgerow patrol which has everything. 

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cm-JnU1DmKg&t=12s&ab_channel=crono23]Tiger hunts[/url] are always fun to watch, here's one in the outskirts of Brest by Crono.

We got some new blood learning the ropes and it is really cool to see their progression. Check out [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WPxzcZjvgiA&ab_channel=LikeableKiwi%28LikeableKiwi%29]LikeableKiwi's fight in Hedgerows [/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/651066b539171439c65a6b43bcb2a323fda354f3.png[/img]

Next patch is about polishing what we got in the game and few interesting additions that have been suggested by the community. I wish you all a very good 2025.

Respectfully,
-urb

notes.title: Mud and Blood 0.4.8 - Silent Night, Violent Night
notes.content:
[h1]Mud and Blood Patch Notes[/h1]
[h3]Version 0.4.8 - Silent Night, Violent Night[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/fee361d140390921d7a7d8d3afcab85716d0036f.png[/img]

Hey folks, urb here! Just in time for the holidays, we've got a fresh patch for you, packed with bug fixes, new features, and plenty of tweaks to keep the Mud and Blood experience evolving. This patch dives deeper into trench warfare mechanics while addressing long-standing quirks and adding some festive surprises. Your feedback and suggestions continue to shape the game, so thank you for being part of this community. Let’s break it down:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/e91e174f689ff83cd874242a0e435ccb04af5682.png[/img]

[h2]New Features and Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Trench Mode Cost Variation: Items in Trench Mode now have varying costs, offering new strategic layers to resource management.
[*] 17 New Cards for Trench Mode: Expand your tactical options with a host of new cards, each designed to shake up gameplay in unique ways.
[*] Panicking Troops Behavior: Troops panicking in Trench 1 can now be summoned back, offering commanders a chance to regroup and stabilize morale.
[*] Historically Accurate Vehicle Call Signs: Thanks to LTHunter’s research, most Allied vehicles now have historically accurate call signs.
[*] Trenchwork Improvements: Roofs of workshops now block airbursts but take double fire damage and stun effects. Be mindful when placing them!
[*] Xmas Special Event! Celebrate the season with a festive event—don’t miss out on limited-time surprises and challenges.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/9f6644bde70714c050c898d202a17e8eb4adcb39.jpg[/img]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed medics in Trench Mode: Medics now heal for 5 HP per tick, with successful heal rolls depending on experience.
[*] Resolved an issue where German stationary units would decrew randomly.
[*] Fixed a crash related to the new Trench Buff (29th, let’s go!) and improved stability.
[*] Corrected spawn locations for Allied soldiers in Trench Mode.
[*] Fixed paratroopers taking damage from spawning in trees.
[*] Resolved a fault with Ranger Training cards in Trench Mode.
[*] Addressed AI behavior where soldiers tossed AT grenades instead of Blendkörpers.
[*] Brick stacks and cars exploding now provide no cover values.
[*] Classic ribbons now display correctly on game over, and Trench Mode no longer brings old Classic ribbons post-reset.
[*] Fixed EW equipment spawning in water on D-Day maps.
[*] Corrected an issue with the Keener achievement in Campaign Mode when reaching exactly 80% in exchanges of fire.

notes.title: Mud and Blood "No Mercy" mega patch
notes.content:
[h1]Mud and Blood Version 0.4.7 - Expect No Mercy[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/82db0352a0b4022332e04f6c97b7b065239818bd.png[/img]

Hey folks, Urb here! It’s been a while, but I’ve been cooking. Today, we’re excited to drop the "Expect No Mercy" mega patch! This release is the work of many talented individuals in the community, including voice actors, testers, and, of course, all of you with your fantastic suggestions. A big thank you to everyone for taking the time to check out or play Mud and Blood. This game has been my passion for nearly 15 years, and I’m truly grateful to share this journey with you all. Thank you, friends!

This is a beast of a patch, so let's dive in:

[h1]Classic Mode Additions:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/5ffaa8b7f8ed70b8445d267ed41c6c93e0ff7f0d.png[/img]

[h3]Grouping hot keys for classic[/h3]We’ve introduced group selection hotkeys in Classic mode for improved quality of life. You can now manage multiple soldiers with ease using Ctrl + 1-6, similar to common RTS games like Warcraft. Simply group select and then press Ctrl + 1 to assign that group to the corresponding key.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/9c6f9b7477211de6692968d9e16725d5fe15dadb.png[/img]

[h3]New stuff and tweaks to existing units [/h3] Commandos now come equipped with [b]frag grenades[/b]. We’ve added a few new defensive positions. [b]Tobruk Cannons[/b] and Pillboxes, augmented by [b]Naval Guns[/b], are now part of your building upgrade arsenal. Shellscrapes are now easier to place and better integrated into the flow of combat, thanks to an increased range limit. We’ve also tweaked their protection values and placement mechanics, ensuring that they provide realistic cover without being overpowered. A new building called the[b] Defensive Position[/b] is available for just 5 TP (which is fairly cheap, although you will need an engineer with a shovel to build it!) and offers a vast array of buffs to soldiers inside.

[h3]New advanced Trench Mode for classic[/h3] This is a complete overhaul, featuring its own ranks and mechanics. It plays similarly to the 1917 flash game from back in the day but with that unmistakable Mud and Blood flair.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/56a9ef0d7c04c77c7c5b72780281e1474d5ca4c7.png[/img]

For some time, I wanted a more competitive feel in Classic matches without altering the original format. After discussions with the community, I decided to create a Trench Mode where players face a predetermined enemy commander. You’ll fight over a large map, with significantly less micro-management of units than in traditional Mud and Blood gameplay. This mode draws inspiration from classic trench games like 1917 and Stickman Trench, as well as the elusive Mud and Blood 1, which was a WWI game.

[h3]Trench mode concept[/h3]In Trench Mode, you’ll move large groups of troops from one trench to another until you seize victory and earn a new unit. The chaos is ramped up to a whole new level as multiple infantry platoons slug it out in the mud. The number of combatants is exponentially larger, and combined with the simplified controls, it becomes a game of strategy and timing rather than micro-management. It’s important to note that the enemy commander also receives TP to buy units and call for support based on cost and their strategy. It would be exciting in the future to have different commanders with unique personalities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/e0c7735fcb0920f18ed692e550136b5f7d5a4c37.png[/img]

[h3]Deck Building Mechanics[/h3] Units come in cards with varying degrees of rarity, with French troops being the most common and airborne troops being the most powerful and rarest. Currently, we offer infantry types and vehicles, providing enough variation to keep things interesting. The trench warfare begins rather mellow, allowing you to learn the mechanics and earn a few solid cards before it ramps up and gets personal.

[h1]New Gear[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/58420dee2a14b175e103d576d0716c4ea68c72a4.png[/img]

[h3]Anti-Tank Rifles[/h3] The idea of a soldier exploding from a hit by a huge-caliber anti-tank rifle definitely fits the Mud and Blood experience. I've added anti-tank rifles for both factions: the Boys Rifle for the Allies and the PZB39 for the Axis. They behave similarly; however, the Boys Rifle has a larger impact explosion and can destroy cover at times. The PZB39 offers excellent range but less damage due to its smaller round. Additionally, 20% of their rounds carry gas, opening up a range of tactical possibilities. It has been entertaining to see how the testers employed these rifles. Each rifle holds 10 rounds and is discarded when empty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/358920c533aaa6a71f734bb175788d7b650b23a0.png[/img]

[h3]Improved Unit Weapons Adjustments:[/h3] Lieutenants and Supply Soldiers have been rebalanced, removing some exotic weapons from their loot tables for a more realistic battlefield haul. Speaking of loot, we’ve ensured that items will not despawn unless there are no soldiers nearby. As long as a soldier is within 600 pixels (half a screen) of an item, it will not despawn.

[h3]New Grenades!![/h3] This patch introduces two new types of grenades. The Blenkorper is a gas grenade that can be thrown onto unsuspecting enemies, rendering them combat ineffective for a few seconds—perfect for mounting an assault on a crowded defensive position.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/78ec448a7caf5f11cd2e3cfd1263f1cecce61f88.png[/img]

The second grenade type is the German Anti-Tank Bundle Grenade. This powerful anti-tank grenade has a lower frag radius but delivers a substantial blast (it also stuns effectively). Use it against armor to deal damage or even destroy them. While it can be tossed at infantry in a pinch, its weight limits its range. For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes or mouth.

[h1]Vehicle Combat Rehaul[/h1]

[h3]Damage to Vehicle Components:[/h3] We’ve been hard at work on a significant change to vehicle combat. Now, vehicles can suffer damage to up to 12 different components, providing a wider range of scenarios and mishaps during battles. It’s all about that immersive experience—things can go south in a heartbeat!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/ef10011fdeaef477af865dc743a50835a9cdf7e1.png[/img]

[h3]Bailing Tank Crews:[/h3] In a new twist to vehicle mechanics, tank crews will now abandon their vehicles if they panic. This change adds an extra layer of vulnerability and unpredictability in tank battles. If the shelling gets too intense or they find themselves outmatched, your or their tank crews may bolt and leave their armored beasts behind, adding a whole new level of strategy and risk when deploying armor. Do you push your tanks hard into enemy lines and risk losing their crew? Or play it safe and keep your armor back, knowing that a panicked crew could mean losing a key asset on the battlefield?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/10a30399303c9f98407ce70a825bc90ae944385f.gif[/img]

[h3]Vehicle related Fixes:[/h3] We’ve significantly improved tank behavior—Churchill tanks now properly signal when they leave the map, and tank coaxial guns won’t generate debug messages during reloads anymore. Tanks have also received a bump in armor-piercing capabilities, while infantry now use Panzerfausts more wisely, so be prepared for smarter enemy tactics when they face your armor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/a9cdb8da5a209643b9afcbc60e0b2469f4075498.png[/img]

[h1]New campaign additions[/h1]

[h3]6 New Battle Conditions for Campaign:[/h3] This patch introduces six new battle conditions: Partisans, Maverick, Tip of the Spear, Rear Echelon, Boys Club, and Link-Up. Partisans have a 3% chance to spawn French Resistance squads when enemy forces are detected—perfect for sneaky sabotage. The Link-Up condition requires you to reach the rendezvous point with the 1st Division in under 5 minutes in the center of the map, or you might anger Gerhardt. Additionally, Maverick units will dive and attack enemy ground targets sporadically, so keep an eye out for your men calling them "birds" to avoid friendly fire scenarios. Rear Echelon and Tip of the Spear conditions adjust the number of enemies on the map based on your progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/b498ee95373e0961b452497fd1381f9a10e4f2da.png[/img]

[h3]Training Mode for Campaign:[/h3] Mud and Blood can be a tough game to get into; it features a myriad of mechanics and is highly randomized. For many players, a compelling war story is better than simply winning. Call it combat narrative or the "Dwarf Fortress of firefights." For new players, the level of aggression and cognitive load can be frustrating, especially since it's not the norm in the industry. To help new players get a grip on the game, it can now be set in Training Mode. This mode significantly lowers the damage from small arms fire, allowing newcomers to understand the types of actions that typically get soldiers killed. Once they feel ready for the gloves to come off, they can switch back to War Mode in the options menu. It’s ironic for a patch called “No Mercy,” but I feel many cool people who would enjoy Mud and Blood haven’t had the chance to experiment with the game before it ramps up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/c19cafd9618b3cc547755e86b7f4443b3735f1bd.png[/img]

[h3]Scrounger command ability[/h3] A new campaign command ability is the Scrounger, which allows the commander to order one of his men to grab a weapon from the ground—whether it's Allied or Axis—and use it for a set number of patrols, based on the card's rarity. This adds a new layer of tactical flexibility, giving commanders the chance to adapt to the battlefield and make use of whatever resources are available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/00925397f64c5066cead35772c8ad8b09f9cbeda.png[/img]

[h3]Campaign Stars and Recognition:[/h3] It’s time your soldiers got some proper recognition for their hard-fought achievements. In campaign mode, soldiers participating in key fights (high intensity in enemy encounters and brutality) will now receive the Campaign Star, a stackable award for their bravery and contribution to victory. The Campaign Star can be awarded multiple times during a campaign.

[h3]New DDAY[/h3] World War II games face a unique challenge because they often begin with D-Day, which for many was the most brutal and pivotal battle of the entire campaign. It’s a balancing act to give this crucial day the respect it deserves while also introducing new players to the game. I wanted Mud and Blood to fully convey the chaos, violence, and unpredictable emergence that defined the Normandy landings. Now, the intensity is at the right level, giving players a taste of the full experience before they push further inland into a more controlled and deliberate advance.

To make this an ultimate brawl, I’ve added additional friendly troops, armor on both sides, and the entire selection of support options, allowing the new Mud and Blood engine to really flex its capabilities.

[h1]New enemies[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/75e473bda022db8f3c534c32d0a0cab803525361.png[/img]

We all agree here, new units are always fun. They add variety visually and create new tactical problems with their equipment and behavior. Well, 0.4.7 brings in four new enemy infantry types.

[h3]Luftwaffe Infantry:[/h3] These defensive specialists make their debut as a unique force on the field. Known for their poor training but remarkable resilience, Luftwaffe infantry are best deployed when you're digging in and holding the line. Although they're less experienced than their Wehrmacht counterparts, these troops benefit from being well-fed, granting them an extra 25 HP over your average German infantry. Their defense-oriented nature makes them tough to dislodge from fortified positions, and they come equipped with their own specialized gear, providing new tactical options in the heat of battle. However, don’t expect them to be quick on their feet—they shine best in defense, so plan accordingly.

[h3]Volksgrenadiers:[/h3] These late-war German heavy infantry units, despite their relatively short training, represent Germany’s last-ditch effort to deploy combat-ready soldiers. They excel when fighting in groups and are equipped with some of the best weaponry that a beleaguered Germany can muster, including the renowned STG44.

I've coded a specific AI for the Volksgrenadiers, and you'll find they prefer to stick together. When in larger groups, their officers will join them, enhancing their buffing capabilities. In terms of behavior, think of them as “Walmart SS.” They’re aggressive and bold but lack the fanaticism of the SS, making them less capable of sustaining tough fights over extended periods. As a result, they can easily falter under prolonged pressure.

However, don’t underestimate them; they’ll come in ready for a slugfest. Armed with heavier weaponry, the Volksgrenadiers will certainly present a serious challenge to your front lines.

[h3]Officers:[/h3] The enemy can now field officers. Their ranks are distributed according to our calculations, including various ranks from young lieutenants to higher-ups. Their appearance will reflect, to the best of our ability, the chances of seeing a given type of officer in the field. Players may encounter plenty of non-staffer officers throughout the campaign, but we love impossible probabilities and can't wait for the first reported field marshal kill.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/2d184b41b72f3043b434b25812c4de8592287ee3.png[/img]

Besides being fun to eliminate, officers are distinct units with the main purpose of buffing and directing nearby troops. The higher their ranks, the more troops they can affect and the more often they will command them. There are eight different order types they can choose from, ranging from basic maneuvers to directing fire or inspiring nearby troops. They work particularly well with troops who operate in tight formations, such as the Volksgrenadiers.

[h3]Pak 36:[/h3] At first glance, this light anti-tank cannon seems too light to be a nuisance. But that 37mm tungsten round can fly pretty far and accurately. Additionally, the crew will dismount and load a muzzle-loaded shaped charge grenade for quite the surprising punch. Being light, the gun can be rolled in or out of action quickly, and its low profile makes it perfect for camouflage ambushes. With the new component damage system, this weapon can still disrupt your advance with a lucky shot.

[h3]New additional AI patterns and existing AI rehaul[/h3] Friendly AI troops can now loot and use items. This includes behaviors for repairing vehicles, rearming nearby Panzerschrecks, and stabilizing bleeding soldiers. They will also use items to the best of their abilities, such as anti-tank devices and extinguishers. This change has led to some exciting emergent gameplay situations during testing.

In the campaign, Volkssturm units are now limited to carrying one lootable item at a time due to their poor nutrition and condition during the war. This small but impactful change keeps the immersion grounded in historical realism. Expect enemies to be a little more strategic with their resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/595191213714c08e2426623b9de493ab736a5074.png[/img]

[h3]New Vehicle:[/h3] Introducing the M20 Utility Vehicle, which now resets skill timers for nearby soldiers when enemies are eliminated. The M20 is a fast-moving Greyhound chassis with a .50 cal on a manual turret, serving as a solid middle ground.

[h3]Final Touches:[/h3] We’ve fixed various issues, from tank sound bugs to proper unlocking of ribbons and achievements. Rain can now extinguish small fires, smoke grenades are more tactical, and we’ve fine-tuned cover values for certain structures to better match their intended function.

Check out the full list of change:


[h3]General Changes and Fixes:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Removed the shell scrape building range limit for players to match enemy capabilities.

notes.title: Mud and Blood Holidays patch is out !!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/a113a8ddb10431d9f97bcad25eee7cffc330e3af.png[/img]

Good day folks urb here with a holiday patch!

[h1]Gib Santa and Earn a Special Ribbon![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/0f79a3004e562a8a433c155499b4d5cc31401c91.png[/img]

As tradition dictates, Santa will make a surprise appearance in your AO during one of your fights. Seize the opportunity to gib the old man and bag yourself a stylish ribbon that enhances your max Tactical Point potential.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/476d8b997fdd9bf4228d9e1c8bac3d36a457d8ae.png[/img]

[h1]Trench Combat Mode for Classic Warfare:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/534657a2782194419839693332b08fff019fae6d.png[/img]

Imagine yourself as the commander, stationed in the front-line trench. Here, the usual 6-man rule takes a back seat, allowing for a more substantial deployment. The catch? Waves of enemies won't yield Tactical Points (TP). How do you earn them, you ask? Well, strategically retreat to the next trench and pocket 20TP. You can repeat this tactical withdrawal up to 5 times. Tempting as it may be to rush to the rear trench for a quick 100 TP, consider the finer points. Without specific ribbons, your TP maxes out at 20, necessitating thoughtful spending during retreats. Moreover, the farther you retreat, the fiercer the Germans get. Trench warfare demands a delicate balance—hold the line as long as possible, then strategically retreat before the inevitable collapse. It adds a unique twist to the economic dynamics in a game of Mud and Blood, offering creative players a canvas for experimentation.

[h1]Rush mode with its unique enemy AI[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/d7043f409bca268d192a77be8c083bd4538e8d2e.png[/img]

Rush mode unlocks after achieving your first promotion in classic, resembling the latest special event. This mode introduces a significantly reduced time between waves, creating a heightened sense of urgency. Notably, the enemy matches the speed of your soldiers. However, the key feature of Rush mode is the integration of its own AI system. The primary goal is to enhance the believability of enemy actions, with AI employing tactics such as utilizing cover, strategically holding and regrouping in staging areas, and occasionally advancing as a cohesive unit. This mode aims to improve overall maneuvering, emphasizing tactics like leveraging concealment for flanking maneuvers and employing mutual cover during movement. The dynamic shift is evident, as the enemy becomes a formidable force early in the game, adopting an aggressive approach. This alteration transforms the focus from building strategies to prioritizing rapid and effective fire output in the short to medium term. It will be interesting to see some of you breaking the puzzle on this one.

[h1]Introducing the Churchill:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/f2268b66828875952f268bbd9eb6de324c55a0a7.png[/img]

The Brits are entering the fray (albeit selectively) with the robust Churchill tank. This beast boasts heavy armor capable of deflecting incoming AT fire, similar to the formidable Tiger. Armed with a fast-firing 6-pounder, it packs a punch against armored targets. The Churchill, though slow, proves difficult to eliminate, offering a nice option to commanders in classic mode. Priced at 20 TP, future upgrades include the fearsome crocodile variant equipped with a flamethrower.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/1e0ede8f9247e38878a87d17ed309acac8f196b2.png[/img]

In campaigns, the Churchill becomes an unstoppable force due to its outstanding armor. However, speed is its Achilles' heel. Deploying a Churchill past the midpoint becomes a gamble, as it may not reach the frontline before being redirected elsewhere. The crew inside enjoys a 4% performance boost, reflecting in the coax and high rate of fire of its main cannon. Overall, the Churchill adds a nice twist for commanders seeking to experiment with a heavy tank.

[h1]New Battle Conditions:[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/05e14097c4fe3938f0bdfe25135f35b96ee55fa7.png[/img]
[h2]Butter Bar:[/h2]
A greenhorn LT straight from the depot has joined a frontline platoon. Inexperienced and tactically challenged, your mission is to safely escort this rookie to the end line. Succeed, and earn x2 XP. Fail, and there's no XP for the day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/f3c1621480028bb1b05be91efaf9db60f7ee229a.png[/img]

[h2]Secondary Duties:[/h2]
Supply headaches persist as they abandon crucial provisions at our lines. Every section must contribute, designating one member to hand-deliver the supplies. Successfully crossing the end line grants x2 XP, but if the supplies are lost, captured, or destroyed, you leave with nothing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/05b6b42b57891eb064269f7701df4f64f0d49e3b.png[/img]

[h2]No Brief:[/h2]
Your mission is clear, but intel on the battlefield is scarce. The other two battle conditions remain unknown. A sharp commander may decipher the current conditions over time and adjust strategies on the fly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/059066c24e6afb189dff7ea49b95a4d16fd67e53.png[/img]

Here is the list of the changes I've made to this version:

[list]
[*] Changed the horse cart to stick around less when empty.
[*] Horsecarts can spawn on roads in the campaign now.
[*] Fixed non-Gold wing holders having the vet save in classic.
[*] Enemy AI can start switching seats in a vehicle now.
[*] Fixed an issue where the rifle grenades would not face the direction they are shot at.
[*] Made the Goliath mines more of a threat. They will now detonate closer to you and can hide when detected.
[*] Altered the deployment options for Enemy AI when an ambush is sprung.
[*] SDKFZ222, which has no gunner, will go back from the front line in an attempt to find a qualified gunner as a replacement.
[*] Reduced Rifle Grenade and Faust morale hit by 5 (from 15 to 10).
[*] Fixing an issue with flamers not facing the right angle on multiple enemies flamer shot.
[*] Fixed an issue where the voice lines of some troops would not match the level of tension related to nearby explosions.
[*] Modified and added some cue tips to improve onboarding.

[*] Deuces will spawn on roads in the campaign.
[*] There is now smoke above light mortars upon firing. This is helpful when looking ahead to locate the mortar crew.
[*] New classic mode: Trench warfare.
[*] Rush mode is now a permanent unlock with an AI that will hide in the trees more and work as a group.
[*] New Campaign Battle Condition: Bad Intel (unknown BCs!!).
[*] New Campaign Battle Condition: Secondary duties (delivery mission).
[*] New Campaign Battle Condition: Butter Bar (Escort mission).

[*] Xmas lights will be deleted if the trench is removed by the map engine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7003c525849438c6904c5802dae03d8d18daab25.png[/img]

Check[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4xqyQ8Td_I&ab_channel=RobertoMagalh%C3%A3es] this insane wave 317 game[/url] by our current Classic Master, Tonny

I'm [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3UjZj5Sj7oQ&ab_channel=Tutle]Following closely the adventures of Tutle[/url] the first documented Campaign Master Mode player. It is always very instructive to watch him play the game with such speed and skill.

Good to check out if you want to get in the fight in Campaign and see how to tackle the beach. In the campaign, this fight is very important to finish with all your men and under 20 min as it will give the DDay ribbon with honour which gives 5xp to all your recruits. A substantial advantage in the long run.

How about this crazy classic finish by Up and that [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ9lGhda6dQ&ab_channel=OpupKK]1000 yards stare guy[/url].

That's it for me folks, I appreciate you all and am thankful you took the time to read my patch notes. Let me know in Discord if you have suggestions, or pop over if you have questions we're always happy to help. I Wish you all a great Christmas and will catch up with you in the next update.

notes.title: Mud and Blood 0.4.4 has dropped!!
notes.content:
Good evening, folks! It's Urb here with a beefy update to share.

But first thanks for playing and checking out on MNB. It warms my heart to know that Mud and Blood is appreciated and it's really cool to watch or hear about some of the crazy fights you guys got yourselves into.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/878d89708f28b44983526e1e9d6fe3534e72e387.png[/img]

Version 0.4.4 has been in the works for a while, and it's jam-packed with exciting content and changes. Let's dive right in:

[b]Trains and Railways:[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/0d0a4081c02210f6301d2a5a1a115442b0853b78.png[/img]

Train wagons can now appear on any railway track in the game, and there are five types:

[b]Regular Flatbed:[/b] These standard wagons don't obstruct line of sight and offer no cover. Keep an eye out for crates with interesting items.

[b]Reinforced Flatbed:[/b] These wagons have been retrofitted to provide protection for infantry units. They can house plenty of enemies and are ideal for defensive purposes.

[b]Box Car:[/b] Box cars offer decent cover and block line of sight. You can fortify them with a sapper to create impromptu strong points.

[b]Tanker:[/b] These generic tankers carry flammable substances and block line of sight. Be cautious—destroying them can set the area ablaze.

[b]Armored Wagon: [/b]By 1943, the Germans had developed the BP42 armored train, equipped with AAA capabilities and a mounted Panzer4 turret. These wagons often house infantry and spell trouble.

[b]Memorial:[/b]
Fallen soldiers from your campaign will be honoured in the memorial, allowing you to pay your respects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/a3a2884f3bdd79de590b58aa73fd969c0a6223ee.png[/img]

[b]UI Changes in the Campaign:[/b]
The soldier portrait now provides more information, including the number of veteran saves and Ranger training.

[b]Particle Engine Improvements:[/b]
Particles now interact with the ground, producing realistic sounds when shells hit different surfaces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7c4cb189e8f3f26c383346e1bcfbfbb2d1ff2c4d.png[/img]

[b]Airborne Challenge:[/b]
In the classic mode, players can now attempt the paratrooper challenge once per promotion. Reach wave 50 with airborne troops to succeed and earn silver wings, increasing the number of troops in an airdrop from 4 to 6. Accumulate enough combat drops, and you might earn rare gold para wings, but remember, you must meet the 82nd's high standards to keep your wings.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8CeQ28Igxc

[b]Gunners and Assistants:[/b]
Qualified gunners can now be assisted by nearby soldiers when reloading or fixing jams, making efficient squad placement crucial.

[b]AI and Loot:[/b]
Enemies can now pick up items from the ground and use them, creating dynamic situations on the battlefield. The enemy AI also cooperates more, such as assisting Panzershreck soldiers or providing first aid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/878d89708f28b44983526e1e9d6fe3534e72e387.png[/img]

[b]Hardcore D-Day:[/b]
This mode intensifies the D-Day experience, removing nerfs on beach troops, adding more defenses, and enabling all enemy support options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/49fcf6f2ca9cc4695e7d4d2ece3ce0dec77c5944.png[/img]

[b]Classic Rush Mode:[/b]
Rush mode shortens the time between enemy waves, creating frantic battles and memorable comebacks.

[b]Sarge Returns:[/b]
The grumpy old Sarge is back, ready to kick some more butt. He now has increased hit points, deals more hand-to-hand damage, and can unpin nearby troops automatically.

[b]Land Mattress:[/b]
The Allies get a new rocket artillery that can fire a volley of 16 rockets every 2 minutes, making it a powerful asset but also a potential hazard if used incorrectly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/e20e95fac8de7076630ce208c3be723ee864dbb8.png[/img]

[b]M1A1 155mm Gun:[/b]
You'll now have access to the Long Tom, a 155mm artillery piece with the ability to switch between different ammunition types, adding versatility to your artillery tactics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7203895effd307381a5ec423b41cf40bdd8a06a7.png[/img]

[b]Nebelwerfer:[/b]
The Germans had a new 6-tube artillery piece for countering enemy artillery, capable of causing chaos on the battlefield.

[b]Deuce:[/b]
A 2 1/2-ton service truck delivers Allied troops through the "big red one" command ability, and you might encounter them on roads during open warfare.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/4a7e04b3a5f9870f62671caedad3beb01c42eb25.png[/img]

[b]17 cm K 18 in MrsLaf:[/b]
This artillery piece fires slowly but packs a punch, making it a significant threat to your artillery units.

[b]Messerschmitt Me 262:[/b]
The enemy has a new plane that flies incredibly fast, called in by firing a red flare. It performs rocket runs, and you can't prevent it with air superiority.

[b]Flak 38:[/b]
A static 20mm flak cannon manned by a single enemy can be found in campaigns and classic mode, often seen in circular trenches.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7a44b7a01fbbf904f95034cdc051199581c0405c.png[/img]

[b]Kettenkrad:[/b]
This German light-tracked vehicle helps transport troops and supplies, and if the driver is killed, your men might loot its contents.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/256e1255bc79f98f0d4dbc43acbc0b23146944ea.png[/img]

[b]Weasel:[/b]
The Allies have their frontline supply vehicle, which delivers supplies directly to your front lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/69868937eeec0608a2d6e58ab381c731448709bc.png[/img]

These are just some of the changes in this update, and you can find the complete list below:

[list]

notes.title: Mud and Blood 0.4.3
notes.content:
Good day folks, urb here welcome to another Mud and Blood patch

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/d2275c534089ec4268b977f014c79a269ef7883e.png[/img]

I'm happy to introduce one of the most significant patches to date for Mud and Blood. This update not only brings two new friendly infantry units to the game, but also a slew of exciting features, fixes and a biome upgrade. But before we dive into the specifics of these mechanics, I want to express once again my heartfelt gratitude to you guys who have been supporting Mud and Blood since its rebirth. Your  support is truly motivating, and I am immensely grateful for your continued enthusiasm it makes creating Mud and Blood such a rewarding hobby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/40ed26b5212815e290cc71ad19264d7d511a454d.png[/img]

So, this patch took a little longer to cook, as the addition of new major mechanics to the game demanded extra polishing and testing (especially the new AI) to ensure a smooth experience in line to what MNB is currently and where it is going! I believe I implemented several new mechanics that will enhance your gameplay and also reinforce what Mud and Blood is set to deliver, a ruthless experience of combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/9f352a049287b36c805d42224c30b7be2b504dbb.png[/img]

Now, let's delve into some of the exciting new features and how they work. There's a lot to cover, so buckle up and get ready for some epic action in Mud and Blood!

[h1] Frenchies!![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/26c63355816bb2d5fd1dcf5c736f507b09a4e959.png[/img]

A classic soldier from the MNB2 the Frenchies are back to the front. Essentially the Frenchies are a low cost/low skill troops.  Some commander consider them good meme material while others have built impressive strategies around their usage. Regardless the French resistance was active part of the of the war and now they are one more additional tactical option for creative commanders out there.

[b]In classic[/b] the Frenchies cost 1 TP and come with a 15 combat skill. Uncommonly a Frenchy can have past military experience or be a veteran of the first war which will increase his combat skill. They are less resilient than well fed and trained soldier with only 75 hp. Their morale can be questionable at times but it is usually the task of the commander on the ground to manage that aspect. If you take care of your Frenchies, they will go the extra mile for you. I must warn the new commanders to be careful if you are tempted to group a large number of Frenchies. Large troop movement tells the enemy where to focus his own troops. (6 men rule)


[b]In campaign[/b] frenchies can be called with a command ability. The abiltiy can call 4 frenchies +1 per rarity tier that will drive, to the best of their abilities, a marked civilian vehicle (fast QRF) to your front line. Frenchies will disembark only if they see enemies, they are like that. They just rather drive around than walk. If you think about it they kinda have a point. If the Vehicle is called and no contact is made within about 3 min the vehicle will leave your AO, probably to go seek a fight somewhere else. Due to their impressive enginuity at procuring material they come to the fight armed with a fairly exotic array of weaponry including older models such as the Chauchat and the Mas36 (see new weapons below)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/7e42e7f94e31a79a5c0c763b23f44aaf47a6dc29.png[/img]

[h1]Airborne[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/274a5c13582f71dab94abd99374b9ffdc7332eee.png[/img]

This patch also has the addition of Airborne troops to Mud and Blood. These highly versatile soldiers have always been a fan favorite due to their superior quality and value for investment. One unique aspect of Airborne troops is that they are deployed via air drop, providing a quick deployment option that carries some inherent risk. Depending on the circumstances, troops may land in unfavorable terrain or dangerously close to enemy forces. Airborne troops are equipped with their own weapons, selected from the airborne-specific arsenal. This diversity in armament may affect the squad's proficiency in certain areas, such as ranged combat or close quarters raiding. Nonetheless, the benefits of having Airborne troops as part of your force outweigh the risks, as they provide unparalleled tactical flexibility and combat prowess. Most of the airborne troops that were fighting alongside of our Division (the 29th) were from the 82nd.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/1a0d1f4a7f2aef41f29dcce3059e02e56f3df47e.png[/img]

[b]In classic[/b] airborne troops can be called to your front lines in exchange for 12 tactical points, bringing in 4 troopers, each with a combat skill of 40 as a standard "no hook" private. It's important to note that the drop can shift slightly to the left or right, so it's crucial to consider the timing and positioning of your front line before making the call. The commander now has the ability to draw a landing zone (LZ) on the ground using the engineer skills, which was introduced in the last patch, allowing for a more precise drop at a specific area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/2051143b736abbfe5757112744a9ad0b5941e26f.png[/img]

[b]In the campaign[/b], Airborne troops are a powerful asset that can be called in using a command ability in the game. When called, a plane will drop an initial group of 4 troopers, with additional troopers added per rarity level, onto your front lines. These AI-controlled troops are known for their high mobility and preference for utilizing vegetation for cover, making them effective in various environments.

Once deployed, the Airborne troops will regroup and either hold their position or make their way towards your location if you are ahead of them. They are cautious when under enemy contact, progressing carefully while utilizing cover. However, it's important to avoid separating too far from them during sustained fights, as leaving only one group to absorb enemy fire may not be ideal.

The Airborne AI may occasionally attempt daring actions, whether rightly or wrongly, when they perceive an opportunity. They are also mindful of not staying out of the fight for too long, as they understand the risk of counterattacks. As a commander, you will need to strategically coordinate and support your Airborne troops to maximize their effectiveness on the battlefield.

[h1]The Wespe[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/867406db1e82ffb295e524ac44d490ab49d91814.png[/img]

The addition of the Wespe, a German mobile artillery vehicle, brings a new dimension to the battlefield. Designed to stay away from direct fire and the front lines, the Wespe engages with powerful HE (high-explosive) rounds against flagged units (visually identified by a friendly unit) that are located far away. The Wespe prioritizes enemy vehicles and other artillery pieces, making it a valuable asset for the Germans, typically called in for counter-battery operations.

As a player using field mobile artillery, you may need to be cautious, as the Wespe poses a potential threat to your own artillery units. Its presence on the battlefield adds a strategic dynamic, requiring players to carefully manage their artillery assets and consider the potential risk of encountering the Wespe in their operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/9047f6bc67db35e9ff2cfa549e5ec6fe8926f469.png[/img]

In my opinion, this is where the gameplay gets interesting. While you're actively engaged in combat at the front lines, the artillery pieces on the map are also engaging in skirmishes to determine who will dominate the field and attempt to destroy the infantry. As a tactical commander, it's crucial to keep an eye on the indirect fire situation in your area of operations (AO), monitor both ends of the map, and anticipate whether you'll need to provide support to your own artillery with command abilities like precision artillery or heavy mortars, or a strategic artillery strike.

Furthermore, we plan to implement more indirect fire units to enhance the meta battle between field artillery, and add variety in artillery pieces and systems to spice up this additional layer of depth. This adds an extra strategic element to the gameplay, requiring careful coordination and decision-making to effectively manage the indirect fire assets and gain an advantage in the battlefield.

[h1]New Weapons[/h1]

Our FFI allies come with an array of salvaged and captured weapons. This variety brings 2 new weapons in the that were used by the French resistance. 

[h3]The Chauchat[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/013be76bf797a63ddb707849fa2f46d910ce0ccf.png[/img]

The Chauchat is a World War I era light machine gun (LMG) that is known for its slow firing rate and less than ideal reliability. It is a relatively heavy weapon to carry, which can be a challenge for soldiers in the field. However, if used effectively, the Chauchat can deliver decent damage with its 8mm round.

After World War I, the Chauchat was either retired by France or distributed to some heavier police and security forces. In some cases, it can still be found in crates or caches. Despite its limitations, the Chauchat holds historical significance as a prominent LMG used during World War I and remains an interesting piece of firearms history.

[h3]MAS36[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/97e53c4f34e258e673386c55ab2f99100c2dae93.png[/img]

The Mas36 is a unique weapon that combines the design of a bolt action rifle with the compactness of a carbine. This gives the MAS a sleek appearance and lower bulk compared to traditional bolt action rifles. However, the range of the MAS may be compromised due to this design choice. Nevertheless, in the hands of a skilled user, it can be a surprisingly fast and effective mid-range secondary marksman rifle.

Despite its age and design, the MAS36 still maintains reasonable reliability and decent firepower. Its combination of unique features makes it an interesting choice for those who value maneuverability and versatility in combat.

[h1]Take charge[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/75c9fad6ae2062734f487c8590bfbc1ede44cfb9.png[/img]

This ability grants the campaign commander temporary command over attached troops in the AO (Area of Operations). The duration of the ability is 1 minute, with an additional 1 minute added per rarity level (thus significantly affected by rarity). Additionally, there is a +10 second bonus length per campaign rank held.

This unique command ability is influenced by factors other than rarity. AI troops (infantry) become selectable and will follow move orders given by the commander. However, they will not act as automatons and may not hold a move order for long if they judge it less than ideal.

This ability proves useful in reorganizing the structure of the advance, assigning AI squads to support specific areas, or saving the lives of allies by guiding them away from ambushes. It can also be employed to direct allies to hold a specific arc while the player's own troops progress. In essence, if the AI troops are positioned effectively and actively engaged in combat, they will tend to hold their position.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/6fb3f288839c8bc6d611a12cec06a6f7c9b41400.png[/img]

[h1]Naval Guns of Brest[/h1]

While advancing towards the port of Brest, the 29th often encountered improvised gun sites consisting of naval battery guns placed on top of fortified locations made of concrete. These naval guns were initially placed to defend against attackers from the sea but were turned inland once the Germans realized the Allies would approach from the interior.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/b359f1cefc8ba10845245f9f2852f875d89148ee.png[/img]

The naval guns are the only neutral unit in the game, which means they can be used by both factions. Whoever occupies the bunker now has control over the artillery piece and can use it against the enemy. In testing, it was entertaining to see the gun changing hands a couple of times during particularly intense fights, creating dynamic scenarios and daring assaults to turn the guns on incoming German armor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/1173ac2e535d169eb0aefefe9a15cbb8ba4d3ebf.png[/img]

Naval guns are pretty sturdy and at times can even still function even when the bunker is destroyed. 

[h1]outskirt Brest[/h1]

The outskirts of Brest are a biome that must be fought through just before entering the city in the campaign. It's a rural area with rolling hills and small hamlets, guarded by gun sites and observation positions. The Germans have dug extensive anti-tank trenches, occupied medieval fortresses, and built hasty defenses on elevated positions to delay the advance to Brest as much as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/82a82dbefe4dbeb62910f0b49557b2c2944d1eac.png[/img]

To reflect the terrain changes in-game, I've added new features to the outskirts, including hills that impede movement and can cause inexperienced troops to fall. This is the first time we've introduced the Z axis in Mud and Blood, so we'll observe how it pans out and make adjustments as needed. Personally, I find it adds depth to the gameplay, as elevation of the terrain now needs to be factored into strategic decisions. Holding the high ground or covering arcs with machine guns becomes a significant factor to consider, just as the Germans will.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/44f2d908b3b1608280fe780c97bee11ddbf9cba0.png[/img]

The map rework introduces a network of procedurally generated medieval fortifications that reflect the unique engineering of these old sites. The 175th will have to navigate and fight through these fully destructible citadels, often outnumbered, in order to clear them. These fortifications come with their own set of props for added fidelity and offer opportunities for intense room-to-room fighting or strategic positioning in an otherwise barren AO.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/ebd33ee64336bb4fdd507f33146906967508b95f.png[/img]

The outskirts of Brest are also currently the special event in classic giving the commanders the opportunity to turn captured naval artillery against the enemy. A satisfying process.

[h1]QoL stuff and functionality:[/h1]

One of the features I'm proud to introduce in this patch is the new 'Halt' command for groups. This was a frequently requested feature in our Discord community and it makes perfect sense. Commanders often needed a quick way to stop the entire squad, especially in situations like minefields or nearby fire. Now you can press 'H' to halt your squad in both modes.

In addition, the tab key now hides portraits and the mini-map, which is helpful when soldiers are close to the edge of the map and you need to navigate in tight spaces without the UI getting in the way. It also allows for capturing cool screenshots.

Furthermore, individual saves are now available! This was also a highly requested feature and it makes perfect sense. You can now reset only one mode, either classic or campaign, or both. Just hit the reset button in the options menu and you will be directed to another menu where you can choose the actions you wish to take.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/fd47c22228643cebf44332dab3e46b2f73468c7b.png[/img]

I've made several additions to the UI, including feedback and sounds, to provide players with auditory or visual confirmation when performing actions or when the game performs certain actions. These improvements were collectively made to enhance clarity, such as the addition of icon notifications when TP is generated by the HQ and preventing system messages from overlapping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39837552/1f5b3ada21df9934eddbd8d50c2481cb0c6427e1.png[/img]

This patch is packed with love and numerous implementations that I'd love to ramble about, but these patch notes are already extensive. Without further ado, let me share the change list.
